evidence: NESTING ARITHMETIC (static, passes). task/task.toml:17-18 [agent] timeout_sec = 7200.0; :21 build_timeout_sec = 600.0; :26-27 [verifier] timeout_sec = 13200.0 -- all byte-identical to the frozen template task.toml and to staged-task-contract.md:53-64. task/tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the template test.sh (diff empty): run_suite wraps `timeout "$budget_sec" rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (test.sh:207), gates budget 1500 (test.sh:213), scored budget 11100 (test.sh:224). Judge timeouts (each judge.toml line 4, equal to template): gates render 600 + constraints 600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack; --max-concurrent-agent 1 so judges run serially and the sum is the right bound). Scored functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack); each single judge < its suite budget. Gates 1500 + scored 11100 = 12600 < 13200. Liveness: 120 x (0.25 s sleep + probe with two 2 s urlopen timeouts) = 30 s typical, worst case about 510 s if the socket hangs; 510 + 12600 = 13110 < 13200, so even the worst-case pre-grading wait plus both full budgets still nests (90 s margin, plus file copy/chmod overhead -- tight but inside). restart_mcp.py:11 HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 > the helper's own 30 s readiness loop + 5 s kill wait (app-restart.sh within test.sh:155-177), and it runs inside the functional judge budget. Agent 7200 s is ample for a node/express/better-sqlite3 app (Colderwater lesson 3: target builds in 5-10 min). build_timeout 600 s covers environment/Dockerfile (apt sqlite3/git + two pinned global npm packages), identical to template; the verifier image (tests/Dockerfile, chromium install with deps) is not governed by build_timeout_sec here and is template-identical. No timeout was changed, so no authorization record is needed. ADEQUACY ('long enough') IS UNMEASURED. The template budgets were sized for a template whose functional judge has 2 criteria; this task's functional judge has 44 criteria (grep -c '^[[criterion' = 44; polish 5, visual 5, gates 1+1) in ONE batched claude-code session (mode = "batched") using z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md defines 14 serial protocols (Z, S, M, L, C, B, N, T, U, K, R, V, A, D, lines 33-59) with 18 mentions of independent contexts, 24 of replays, 5 timed-observation definitions (each up to 15 s and up to 3 attempts per prompt.md:21), one restart_app, and a 'report every step' requirement (prompt.md:23-25). Protocol B alone (prompt.md:43) has 16 numbered steps, most with UI action + replay + independent-context readback; protocol R (prompt.md:53) demands ~7 replays for each of two roles plus ~10 anonymous replays with HTTP status recorded; protocol T/U add many cross-session timed observations. A rough count is several hundred Playwright MCP tool turns; at a plausible 10-30 s per LLM+browser turn that is roughly 3000-12000 s against a 9000 s functional judge timeout -- i.e. the band straddles the limit. raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and every entry is labelled 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'; the scripted golden harness duration is not LLM judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY.md:25, Colderwater lesson 19). prompt.md:61 maps an exhausted budget to binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation', which still scores 0 in reward, and Colderwater lesson 11 notes judge timeouts zero a dimension; a functional dimension at 0 fails the functional floor 0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11), zeroing the whole reward. So whether a correct app can be fully graded inside 9000 s is the decisive open question for this row, and no measurement exists. Plausible broken app that could pass: none via timeouts -- a hung or slow broken app only times out to 0. Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app with slower renders or larger DOM snapshots (e.g. long conversation histories in protocol T/U) makes each judge turn slower and could push the 44-criterion batched session past 9000 s, scoring a conforming submission 0 for a harness reason. Lesson-pattern sweep for this row: lesson 7/14 timed observations with up to two repeats exist (prompt.md:21) and add bounded wall time (max 3 x 15 s each); lesson 9 per-step reporting increases output length/time; lesson 10 assembled functional prompt is about 48 KB (prompt.md 20517 B + judge.toml 25629 B + app_context 1921 B), under 128 KB, not a timeout issue but larger context slows each turn; lesson 11 judge infra timeouts zero a dimension -- relevant and unmeasured.
counterexample: Not demonstrated (no run). Hypothetical but concrete: the golden solution, graded by the configured claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx functional judge, needs more than 9000 s to walk protocols Z..D with all replays, independent contexts and timed observations; RewardKit times the functional judge out, the dimension records 0 (or every remaining criterion is 'NOT EXERCISED' = 0), the functional floor 0.05 fails and the conforming app's reward is 0.
suggested_fix: Run one full configured verifier (test.sh with the real judge) on the frozen golden and record the functional judge wall time and per-suite durations in a hash-bound workload record; if functional exceeds about 70% of 9000 s, first trim redundant browser work (e.g. duplicate replay legs in protocols B and R) together with matching public scope, and only with explicit recorded authorization raise the functional timeout and scored/verifier budgets in step, staying below five hours and noting that test.sh budgets are template-controlled.
